comments.selected_text: All three examples in Fig. 6 enter the pronounced rise with negative raw-gradient cosine. During the rise, the gra- dient norm increases sharply and ηbκ exceeds two before the loss maximum. Momentum norms also grow, with model- dependent timing relative to the raw gradient. In the Trans- former, the first crossing of two within the excursion is at state 788, when loss is only 0.40% above its pre-rise level. The +10% crossing follows at 790; raw-gradient and momentum norms reach their event maxima at 792 and 793, before loss peaks at 794. The diagnostic thus precedes the pronounced spike and its maximum, while the first small loss increase has already occurred. The descent separates the models. ResNet and Transformer move toward positive gradient and momentum cosines, lower projected change and a comparatively smooth loss decline. The MLP continues to oscillate: raw cosine remains mostly nega- tive while momentum cosine changes sign, and loss and norms decrease through repeated rebounds. Recovery therefore need not require every raw-gradient pair to become constructive. These examples associate the developing loss spike with gradient reversal and rapid norm amplification, even though the parameter steps are adaptive. An above-two value marks a strong local gradient response consistent with the observed excursion; it is not proof of a linear instability of Adam. The early response suggests an opportunity to anticipate further growth and intervene. Whether it supplies a reliable trigger, or whether acting on it improves training, requires evidence beyond selected examples.
